    The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their significant-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    It has been revealed that “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” stated head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the latest season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    It has been revealed that he lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

    Industry observers note that richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

    Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

    Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

    This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

    Industry observers note that bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

    Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

    De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will swiftly look a lot different. There are more upcoming faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

    Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

    But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

    Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that massive-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his upcoming-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

    Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

    Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

    Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

    Industry observers note that his team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

    It has been revealed that “You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

    Sources indicate that “We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

    “I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

    According to recent reports, “Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

    “We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] upcoming players but we have to put something more.

    According to recent reports, “We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

    Sources indicate that we had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

    It has been revealed that it was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of latest players. To become a team I mentioned before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

    We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

    Sources indicate that really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can rapidly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

    Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

    It has been revealed that that’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

    Recent findings suggest that that is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s upcoming leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    Industry observers note that de Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    Industry observers note that spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the significant boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    #131559. Connor Bedard injury: Blackhawks star's latest issue shines light on a stalled out rebuild in Chicago

    Connor Bedard injury: Blackhawks star's latest issue shines light on a stalled out rebuild in Chicago

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An awful start for the Chicago Blackhawks only got worse on Monday night when the team unveiled that captain and superstar forward Connor Bedard would miss four months after undergoing right shoulder surgery.
    • 17, Bedard injured his shoulder on a face-off and left the ice in a lot of discomfort.
    • According to recent reports, bedard missed the first two weeks of the season while recovering from surgery on his left shoulder in the offseason.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An awful start for the Chicago Blackhawks only got worse on Monday night when the team unveiled that captain and superstar forward Connor Bedard would miss four months after undergoing right shoulder surgery.

    On Nov. 17, Bedard injured his shoulder on a face-off and left the ice in a lot of discomfort. After deliberating whether to rehab the shoulder or get surgery to repair the glitch, Bedard opted for the latter half. That will sideline him longer now, but it could provide a more permanent fix.

    According to recent reports, bedard missed the first two weeks of the season while recovering from surgery on his left shoulder in the offseason. The Blackhawks captain suffered that injury during summer training -- and that also occurred on a seemingly innocuous play.

    In a recent development, even after Bedard's initial injury, Chicago hoped that the 2026-27 season would be a step in the right direction amid a lengthy rebuild. Instead, the team is on track to finish with fewer points this year than last year -- despite playing two more games.

    The Blackhawks are 8-14-2, which is good for 30th place in the NHL. Only the aging Pittsburgh Penguins and actively tanking Vancouver Canucks sit below them. The prospects Chicago has drafted in recent years haven't shown adequate process at the NHL level, and they've got no veteran support around them.

    With Bedard out for an extended period of time, the Blackhawks must re-assess their long-term vision.

    It has been revealed that when healthy, Bedard has shown that he can be a true superstar. The 21-year-old has 82 goals and 139 assists in 234 career games, and he began the 2025-26 season on a torrid pace before, well, suffering a shoulder injury.

    Sources indicate that and therein lies the biggest question about Bedard's future as a true force in the NHL. Is this just bad luck, or will his lack of durability prevent him from reaching the potential that's evident when the puck is on his stick? Chicago can only hope its the former, but this isn't the first time Bedard has missed significant time due to injury.

    This is now Bedard's fourth NHL season, and he's played 70-plus games just once. That was in the 2024-25 season, when he played all 82 games and tallied 67 points.

    Last season, a right shoulder injury forced him to miss 13 games and snuffed out his tremendous start. Months later, Bedard injured his left shoulder after taking a spill during summer workouts. That prompted one surgery, and his latest right shoulder injury prompted another procedure less than five months later.

    I'm certainly not a doctor, but two shoulder surgeries that close together seems concerning, especially for how much the Blackhawks have invested in Bedard.

    It has been revealed that in 2022-23, the franchise completely demolished its roster in hopes of landing the No. 1 overall pick. It worked, and Chicago got to draft Bedard, the consensus top prospect in the class. This past summer, Bedard and the Hawks agreed to a five-year contract extension worth $75 million.

    Sources indicate that if Bedard gets healthy and plays anywhere near his peak, that will be a discount. If injuries continue to limit him, the Blackhawks will have a serious problem on their hands, but that probably goes without saying.

    Even with Bedard in the mix, the Blackhawks' rebuild wasn't going particularly well. Chicago hasn't finished above .500 since the 2019-20 season, which was cut short due to the COVID-19 pandemic and was three years before they selected Bedard in the 2023 NHL Draft.

    The upshot of all that stinking is that the Hawks stocked up on premium draft capital. With that, they've built what should and exciting young core for the franchise. Not including Bedard, Chicago has seven skaters who were selected in the top 50 picks of the last five drafts.

    Kantserov has shown scoring touch at the NHL level, Nazar has been inconsistent and flashed upside and Rinzel has started to show signs of progress on the back end. Other than that, none of those young guns are ready for primetime. That's not say they will never get there. In particular, Frondell and Levshunov have the tools to get there.

    It's just that the results have been really ugly to this point. According to Natural Stat Trick, the Blackhawks rank 30th in expected goals share at 42.5%. The team's minus-32 goal differential ranks 31st in the NHL. To put it more succintly, Chicago is getting what it deserves more often than not.

    With Bedard out for the next four months, it's time to see who can sink and who can swim. Stop playing 37-year-old Ian Cole almost 20 minutes per game and let defensive prospects see the ice more. Tyler Bertuzzi has been incredibly ineffective, and his contract is moveable. Trade him to a contender and open up another spot for a young player in the top six.

    In a recent development, if the team doesn't make any progress over the last 60 games of the season, it may be time for a wholesale changes at the top. General manager Kyle Davidson was tasked with orchestrating a rebuild that's going nowhere quickly. Jeff Blashill is 37-53-16 behind the Blackhawks' bench, and he's 241-314-88 in his coaching career.

    According to recent reports, if Chicago continues to flail at the bottom of the standings, how much worse could it possibly get? A latest set of eyes in the front office and a new voice in the locker room wouldn't be the worst ideas.
